t: You're at the site of the London Fever Hospital, on Liverpool Road in Islington. It was a voluntary hospital, paid for by public donations, and one of the first fever hospitals in the country. It treated people with infectious disease at a time when that was a constant fear in the city. Arthur Ellis Durham, a British physician, died here in 1893, aged only twenty-eight. The record doesn't say more about the circumstances, so I'll leave it there.
